title: Highlighting with Span
prompt:
A <span> marks a piece of text inside a sentence without starting a new block — perfect for highlighting a word or phrase.

In the paragraph below, wrap these words in spans (keep the rest of the sentence unchanged):

  • Wrap important in <span class="important">…</span>
  • Wrap quietly in <span class="quiet">…</span>
  • Wrap surprise in <span id="surprise">…</span>

CSS for those hooks is already provided (read-only). After you Run, the three words should look styled differently.

html.starter: This is an important tip: speak quietly, then shout surprise!

tests.name: HTML validates
tests.feedback: Fix the HTML validation errors shown in the test details.

tests.name: span.important says important
tests.feedback: Wrap the word important in important.

tests.name: span.quiet says quietly
tests.feedback: Wrap the word quietly in quietly.

tests.name: #surprise says surprise
tests.feedback: Wrap the word surprise in surprise.

tests.name: Exactly three spans
tests.feedback: Use exactly three <span> elements — one for each highlighted word.

solution.html: This is an important tip: speak quietly, then shout surprise!
